newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Dec 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
PAY THEN PAY AGAIN ON TUBE

Passengers face the threat of another fare increase on the London Underground, this would come on top of next month's annual fares rise. The second increase could be as much as four or five per cent. The increase was proposed due the financial crisis at LU caused by a cut in Government funding and Jubilee Extension overspend.

Airbus is planning to hasten their plans to become a limited company, following Boeing's $13.3 billion takeover of McDonnell Douglas. Airbus chairman Edzard Reuter admitted, "The Boeing-McDonnell Douglas merger will force us to consider moving quicker." The merged company will tower over competitors -- as a City analyst remarked, "These guys will have all the resources to go after any aircraft project they want."
STERLING FIRMS ON WARNING FROM MAJOR

Cautious words from John Major over joining a single currency helped the pound remain firm on foreign exchanges today. Major also reaffirmed that Britain would adopt a "wait and see" attitude towards the move. A London trader remarked that sterling will benefit from the underlying strength of the British economy.
FIVE BLN STG RAIL BURDEN FALLS ON TAX PAYER

The taxpayer will fork out over five billion stg to the private sector rail companies. OPRAF report that the Treasury will have to find 3.7 billion stg in rail subsidies. The biggest winners include Compagnie Generale des Eaux, Prism and Virgin. National Express will have to pay the Treasury to run the Gatwick Express and Midland Mainline.
